translation_en: Muslim narrated to us; Hisham narrated to us; Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I was giving Abu Talhah, Abu Dujanah, and Suhayl ibn al-Bayda a mixture of unripe dates and ripe dates to drink when wine was prohibited. I threw it away while I was serving them and was the youngest of them. At that time, we considered it wine. Amr ibn al-Harith also said: Qatadah narrated to us that he heard Anas.

Abu Asim narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ata informed me that he heard Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade mixing raisins with dates, unripe dates with fresh ripe dates, and dates with raisins when making an infusion.

Muslim narrated to us; Hisham narrated to us; Yahya ibn Abi Kathir informed us, from Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade combining dates with fresh, nearly ripe dates, and dates with raisins. Each should be steeped separately.

Abdan narrated to us; Abdullah informed us; Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Said ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: On the night the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was taken on the Night Journey, a cup of milk and a cup of wine were brought to him.

Al-Humaydi narrated to us: I heard Sufyan; Salim Abu al-Nadr informed us that he heard Umayr, the freedman of Umm al-Fadl, narrate from Umm al-Fadl, who said: The people were uncertain whether the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was fasting on the Day of Arafah. I sent him a vessel containing milk, and he drank it. Sufyan sometimes related it this way: The people were uncertain whether the Messenger of Allah was fasting on the Day of Arafah, so Umm al-Fadl sent it to him. When the chain is traced back, he said: It is from Umm al-Fadl.

Qutaybah narrated to us; Jarir narrated to us, from al-Amash, from Abu Salih and Abu Sufyan, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: Abu Humayd brought a cup of milk from al-Naqi to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. He said to him, “Would you not cover it, even by placing a stick across it?”

Umar ibn Hafs narrated to us; my father narrated to us; al-Amash narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Salih—I think he mentioned it from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him—who said: Abu Humayd, a man from the Ansar, came from al-Naqi carrying a vessel of milk for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. The Prophet said, “Would you not cover it, even by placing a stick across it?” Abu Sufyan also narrated to me from Jabir, from the Prophet, the same report.

Mahmud narrated to me; al-Nadr informed us; Shu'bah informed us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came from Mecca with Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr said: We passed a shepherd while the Messenger of Allah was thirsty. Abu Bakr said: I milked a small amount into a cup, and he drank until I was satisfied that he had had enough. Suraqah ibn Ju'shum came to us on horseback. The Prophet supplicated against him, so Suraqah asked him not to do so and to let him return. The Prophet did so.

Abu al-Yaman narrated to us; Shuayb informed us; Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Excellent charity is a milch camel that gives abundant milk as a gift, and a milch sheep that gives abundant milk as a gift: it goes out in the morning with one vessel and returns in the evening with another.”

Abu Asim narrated to us, from al-Awzai, from Ibn Shihab, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, drank milk, rinsed his mouth, and said, “It contains fat.”

Ibrahim ibn Tahman reported from Shu'bah, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “I was taken up to the Lote Tree, and there were four rivers: two visible rivers and two hidden rivers. The visible ones were the Nile and the Euphrates, while the hidden ones were two rivers in Paradise. Three cups were brought to me: one containing milk, one honey, and one wine. I took the one containing milk and drank it. I was told, ‘You have chosen the natural way, you and your community.’” Hisham, Said, and Hammam reported from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from Malik ibn Sasaa, from the Prophet, a similar account about the rivers, but they did not mention the three cups.

Abdullah ibn Maslamah narrated to us, from Malik, from Ishaq ibn Abdullah, who heard Anas ibn Malik say: Abu Talhah had more date palms and wealth than any other man of the Ansar in Medina. His most beloved property was Bayruha, which faced the mosque. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to enter it and drink its pleasant water. Anas said: When the verse was revealed, “You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love” (Quran 3:92), Abu Talhah stood and said: “Messenger of Allah, Allah says, ‘You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love,’ and the property I love most is Bayruha. I give it in charity for Allah, hoping for its reward and provision with Allah. So place it wherever Allah directs you.” The Messenger of Allah said: “Well done! That is profitable wealth” (or “wealth that will bring profit”; Abdullah was unsure). “I have heard what you said, and I think you should give it to your closest relatives.” Abu Talhah said: “I will do that, Messenger of Allah.” He then divided it among his relatives and his paternal cousins. Ismail and Yahya ibn Yahya reported the wording “wealth that will bring profit.”

Abdan narrated to us; Abdullah informed us; Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, informed me that he saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, drink milk. He went to his home, milked a sheep, and mixed water from the well with milk for the Messenger of Allah. He took the cup and drank. Abu Bakr was on his left and a Bedouin on his right. He gave the remaining drink to the Bedouin, then said, “The one on the right, then the one on the right.”

Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us; Abu Amir narrated to us; Fulayh ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Said ibn al-Harith, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with them both: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came to a man from the Ansar with a companion. He said to him, “If you have water that has spent the night in a waterskin, bring it; otherwise, we will drink directly from the water.” The man was directing water in his garden. He said: “Messenger of Allah, I have water that spent the night. Come to the shaded shelter.” He went with them, poured water into a cup, and milked a domesticated sheep into it. The Messenger of Allah drank, then the man who had come with him drank.

Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Abu Usamah narrated to us and said: Hisham informed me, from his father, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, liked sweet foods and honey.

Abu Nuaim narrated to us; Misar narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, from al-Nazzal, who said: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, came to the gate of al-Rahbah and drank while standing. He said: Some people dislike drinking while standing, but I saw the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, do just as you have seen me do.

Adam narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us; Abd al-Malik ibn Maysarah narrated to us: I heard al-Nazzal ibn Sabrah relate from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that after praying the noon prayer he sat in the open area of Kufa to attend to people's needs until the time for the afternoon prayer arrived. Water was brought to him. He drank, washed his face and hands, wiped his head and feet, then stood and drank the remaining water while standing. He said: Some people dislike drinking while standing, but the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did just as I have done.
Abu Nuaim narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Asim al-Ahwal, from al-Shabi, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, drank while standing from Zamzam.

Malik ibn Ismail narrated to us; Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us; Abu al-Nadr informed us, from Umayr, the freedman of Ibn Abbas, from Umm al-Fadl bint al-Harith, who said: She sent the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, a cup of milk while he was standing on the evening of Arafah. He took it in his hand and drank. Malik added, from Abu al-Nadr: He was on his camel.

Ismail narrated to us: Malik narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was brought milk mixed with water. A Bedouin was on his right and Abu Bakr on his left. He drank, then gave it to the Bedouin and said, “The one on the right; the one on the right.”

Ismail narrated to us: Malik narrated to me, from Abu Hazim ibn Dinar, from Sahl ibn Sad, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was brought a drink and drank from it. A boy was on his right and elders were on his left. He said to the boy, “Will you permit me to give it to these people?” The boy said, “By Allah, Messenger of Allah, I would not give anyone preference over me regarding my share from you.” So the Messenger of Allah placed it in his hand.

Yahya ibn Salih narrated to us; Fulayh ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Said ibn al-Harith, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with them both: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, entered upon a man from the Ansar with a companion. The Prophet and his companion greeted him, and the man returned the greeting, saying, “May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, Messenger of Allah.” It was a hot hour, and he was directing water in his garden. The Prophet said, “If you have water that spent the night in a waterskin, bring it; otherwise, we will drink directly from the water.” The man was directing water in his garden. He said: “Messenger of Allah, I have water that spent the night in a waterskin.” He went to the shaded shelter, poured water into a cup, then milked a domesticated sheep into it. The Prophet drank and repeated it; then the man who had come with him drank.

Musaddad narrated to us; Mutamir narrated to us, from his father, who said: I heard Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, say: I was standing among the people, giving them fadikh to drink; my paternal uncles were there, and I was the youngest of them. It was said, “Wine has been prohibited.” He said, “Pour it away.” So we poured it away. I asked Anas: What was their drink? He said: Fresh ripe dates and unripe dates. Abu Bakr ibn Anas said: That was their wine, and Anas did not object. One of my companions told me that he heard Anas say: That was their wine at the time.

Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us; Rawh ibn Ubadah informed us; Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: Ata informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “When night falls—or when evening comes—keep your children close, for the devils spread out then. After an hour of the night has passed, let them go. Close the doors and mention Allah's name, for Satan does not open a closed door. Tie the mouths of your waterskins and mention Allah's name. Cover your vessels and mention Allah's name, even if you place something across them, and extinguish your lamps.”

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us; Hammam narrated to us, from Ata, from Jabir, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Extinguish the lamps when you go to sleep, close the doors, tie the mouths of waterskins, and cover food and drink” (I think he also said), “even with a stick placed across it.”

Adam narrated to us; Ibn Abi Dhib narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah, from Abu Said al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade drinking by bending back the mouths of waterskins to drink directly from them. [The narrator explained:] That means breaking or folding their mouths open so one can drink from them.

Muhammad ibn Muqatil narrated to us; Abdullah informed us; Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah informed me that he heard Abu Said al-Khudri say: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbid drinking by bending back the mouths of waterskins. Abdullah said: Mamar or someone else said that this means drinking directly from their openings.

Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us; Ayyub narrated to us. Ikrimah said to us: Shall I tell you some brief reports that Abu Hurairah narrated to us? The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade drinking from the mouth of a waterskin or water container, and forbade a person from preventing his neighbor from inserting a wooden beam into his house.

Musaddad narrated to us; Ismail narrated to us; Ayyub informed us, from Ikrimah, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade drinking from the opening of a waterskin.

Musaddad narrated to us; Yazid ibn Zuray narrated to us; Khalid narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade drinking from the opening of a waterskin.
